History:
• 2-day history of constant, dull ache in lower abdomen (below umbilicus) associated with nausea and feeling hot/sweaty (subjective fever).  
• No vomiting.  
• Bowel habit: constipated 1 week ago; passed stool yesterday; currently having regular bowel motions. No diarrhoea.  
• Urinary: drinking large amounts of water; notices increased urinary frequency but denies dysuria, urgency, foul smell, or flank pain.  
• Gynecologic: Last menstrual period ≈3 weeks ago; expects next period soon. Mild pink spotting over the last couple of days. Sexually active with one partner; etonogestrel implant (Implanon) in situ. No vaginal discharge, dyspareunia, or known pregnancy.  
• No light-headedness, syncope, or shoulder-tip pain.  
• No recent trauma, travel, or sick contacts.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic illnesses: None reported.  
• Surgical history: Not recorded.  
• Medications: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Drug allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction not specified).  
• Family history: Brother with type 1 diabetes; otherwise non-contributory.  
• Social: Non-smoker, lives with boyfriend, no alcohol/smoking details recorded.

Physical Examination:
• Tele-consultation only; no vitals or physical findings documented.  
• General appearance reported: feeling hot/sweaty, otherwise alert.  
• Abdominal, pelvic, cardio-respiratory, neurological exams: Not recorded.

Impression:
Constant lower-abdominal pain with nausea and mild spotting in a reproductive-age woman on an implant – pregnancy and pelvic/urinary pathology need exclusion.

Consistent top differentials (from DDx and transcript):
1. Urinary tract infection (cystitis ± early pyelonephritis) – lower-abdominal discomfort, urinary frequency, subjective fever.  
2. Early intra-uterine or ectopic pregnancy – pelvic pain, spotting, nausea despite contraceptive implant.  
3. Pelvic inflammatory disease – lower-abdominal ache, feverish sensation, inter-menstrual spotting, sexually active.

Management Plan:
• Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for physical examination.  
  – Pregnancy test (urine ± serum β-hCG) to rule out intra-uterine/ectopic pregnancy.  
  – Urinalysis ± urine culture to assess for UTI.  
  – Pelvic examination and swabs if PID suspected.  
• Consider basic blood work (CBC, CRP) and abdominal/pelvic ultrasound if clinically indicated after exam.  
• Safety-net advice: If pain intensifies, develops light-headedness, true fever, vomiting, syncope, or heavy bleeding, attend urgent care or emergency department immediately.  
• Continue adequate hydration; may use simple analgesia (e.g., acetaminophen) if needed – dose not discussed.  
• Follow-up: GP appointment today; further follow-up arranged based on initial results.

Patient Summary:
28-year-old woman with 2 days of constant lower-abdominal ache, nausea, subjective fever, increased urinary frequency, and recent spotting. No dysuria or GI upset currently. Needs urgent in-person assessment to rule out UTI, pregnancy (including ectopic), and pelvic infection.

Key Takeaways:
• Attend face-to-face GP appointment today for examination, pregnancy test, and urine tests.  
• Seek immediate care if pain worsens, you feel faint, develop true fever, heavy bleeding, or persistent vomiting.

Next Steps:
• Same-day GP visit.  
• Point-of-care urine pregnancy test and urinalysis.  
• Further labs/imaging per in-person findings.  
• Arrange follow-up call/appointment to review results and adjust treatment.
